legacy_migration.trigger: A shared workplace deadline creates several simultaneous pressure nodes, but the audience must understand one changing priority at a time
legacy_migration.directing_decision: Treat camera travel as an attention handoff: hold until the current state is legible, then let an entrant, exit, gaze, or line of movement pull the camera to the next zone
legacy_migration.coverage: Mobile master with deliberate close/medium re-anchors; do not drift continuously at one distance
legacy_migration.blocking: Have the next priority enter or become visible before the camera abandons the current one
legacy_migration.pacing_edit: Use dwell and travel duration as rhythm; a cut is optional, not forbidden
legacy_migration.sound: UNKNOWN in this source; candidate sound lead requires later evidence
legacy_migration.applicability: Strongest in connected practical spaces with rehearsable routes and causal overlap
legacy_migration.failure_mode: Camera arrives late, leaves before a reaction lands, or follows movement that does not change story priority
legacy_migration.counterexample: If a decisive state change is a small object or precise hand action hidden by bodies, use an insert or anchored close view instead of preserving the master
legacy_migration.unknown: Exact audio cueing and invisible stitches
legacy_migration.ai_risk: HIGH: multi-character identity drift, path drift, and background-state resets
legacy_migration.fallback: Break the route into short shots at doorway crossings, body wipes, whip reframes, or brief blank-wall occlusions while preserving zone order and eyelines

legacy_migration.applicability: Procedural, kitchen, newsroom, workshop, emergency-response, or backstage scenes
legacy_migration.failure_mode: Every revisit looks spatially new, so the audience reads teleportation rather than accumulating pressure
legacy_migration.counterexample: A one-off emotional confession in a neutral room may benefit from sustained stillness instead of repeated zone cycling
legacy_migration.unknown: Exact prop/order state outside sampled frames
legacy_migration.ai_risk: HIGH: prop count, repeated extras, costume identity, and floor-plan continuity
legacy_migration.fallback: Use a fixed floor-plan package, one anchor image per zone, explicit entrance/exit directions, and a continuity ledger; reduce background workers before reducing causal anchors

legacy_migration.trigger: An operational conflict has produced an exit or irreversible relational withdrawal
legacy_migration.directing_decision: After the exit, reduce bodies and movement, hold on the person left behind, then allow the camera to settle on an emptied work surface or rule-bearing environment
legacy_migration.coverage: One reaction hold plus one empty-space aftermath; either can remain in the master or become two shots
legacy_migration.blocking: Give the departing person a readable route; keep the remaining person's change of posture visible before leaving the face
legacy_migration.pacing_edit: Lengthen dwell after the exit; avoid immediately restarting ensemble motion
legacy_migration.applicability: Rupture, failed leadership, abandonment, shock, or quiet defeat where aftermath matters
legacy_migration.failure_mode: Empty space arrives before the exit is understood, or becomes decorative because no prior spatial anchor was established
legacy_migration.counterexample: If the story requires immediate rescue, chase, or damage control, lingering on empty space weakens urgency
legacy_migration.unknown: Audible exit cue and exact verbal turn
legacy_migration.ai_risk: MEDIUM: generated actors may disappear without a coherent exit or leave inconsistent props
legacy_migration.fallback: Use three bounded shots: departure in shared frame, held reactor, then the previously established empty work anchor

legacy_migration.trigger: A literary scene implies continuous real-time pressure, but generation cannot reliably sustain long multi-character action
legacy_migration.directing_decision: Preserve the functions of continuity — shared clock, stable geography, carried prop states, and uninterrupted escalation — without requiring a literal 17-minute generation
legacy_migration.coverage: A chain of short masters, two-shots, reactions, and only necessary process inserts connected by motivated joins
legacy_migration.blocking: Assign one start/end mark and one state change per generated shot; carry entrances/exits across adjacent shots
legacy_migration.pacing_edit: Keep a continuous timing ledger and avoid resetting emotional intensity between clips
legacy_migration.sound: Use a continuous ambience/pressure bed only after sound evidence is separately validated
legacy_migration.applicability: Any model-neutral pipeline with limited clip duration, identity stability, or complex blocking capacity
legacy_migration.failure_mode: Treating “one take” as a style target creates unusable duration, identity drift, missing workers, and discontinuous work states
legacy_migration.counterexample: When a production can safely rehearse and capture a real continuous take, fragmentation may lose embodied spatial pressure; that is a production choice, not a default law
legacy_migration.unknown: Provider-specific maximum duration and sound-generation capability remain outside this evidence
legacy_migration.fallback: Split at observed body wipes, doors, whip moves, foreground blocks, and brief empty surfaces; retain the same zone order and escalation checkpoints
legacy_migration.confidence: HIGH for fallback necessity; MEDIUM for exact shot recipe
